The studio was silent, save for the soft hum of the air conditioner and the gentle breathing of twelve people attempting to achieve enlightenment. Jim, a man whose idea of flexibility was reaching for the remote without standing up, sat in the back row. He had intended to join the "Intro to Stretching" class, but a misread sign on the door led him here, to "Advanced Asana & Acoustic Resonance."

The instructor, a serene woman named Serenity who hadn’t blinked in forty minutes, raised a hand. "Now," she whispered, "we move into the Pose of the Silent Wind. Breathe in... and release any tension."

Jim, eager to blend in, closed his eyes and focused on his core. He thought he was releasing tension. In reality, he was releasing a pressurized cloud of gas that had been building since his lunchtime burrito. The sound was not a whisper. It was a trumpet blast, loud enough to rattle the water bottles in the front row.

The class froze. Eyes snapped open. Serenity’s eye twitched.

"Jim," she said, her voice dangerously calm. "Is that... part of the pose?"

"I think I'm just really relaxed," Jim squeaked, trying to maintain a lotus position while his face turned the color of a ripe tomato.

"Very well," Serenity said, turning to the class. "It seems Jim has discovered the Pose of the Thundering Bull. Let us all join him in this... unique expression of energy."

The class groaned. Jim, sweating profusely, decided to double down. He shifted his weight, attempting to transition into the Downward Dog. As he lifted his hips, gravity and physics conspired against him. Another sound erupted, this one longer, more resonant, and distinctly melodic. It sounded like a tuba falling down a flight of stairs.

A student in the front row, a serious yogi named Greg, slowly turned around. "Jim," he said, "are you playing an instrument?"

"No!" Jim cried, trying to hold a pose that was now physically impossible due to the sheer volume of his own emissions. "I'm just... finding my center!"

"Your center is currently located in the hallway," Greg muttered.

Serenity clapped her hands once, sharply. "Enough! Jim, please step outside. You are disrupting the chakras of the entire room."
